nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Count forward and backward by 1s, 2s, 5s and 10s from any starting point to at least 120
hintLadder: Point to each number as you count.
Look for the pattern in the ones digit.
Use the hundreds chart to keep track.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Read, write and represent two-digit numbers
hintLadder: Count the tens blocks first.
How many ones are left over?
Write the tens digit first, then the ones digit.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Compare and order two-digit numbers using < = > symbols
hintLadder: Compare the tens digits first.
If tens are equal, look at the ones digit.
The arrow on < points to the smaller number.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Represent and solve addition problems within 20 using strategies including counting on and making 10
hintLadder: Start with the bigger number and count on.
Can you make 10 first and then add the rest?
Use the ten frame to see the groups.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Represent and solve subtraction problems within 20 using strategies including counting back and think addition
hintLadder: Start at the bigger number and count back.
What addition fact could help you?
Use the number line to jump backwards.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Identify and describe the features of familiar 2D shapes and 3D objects
hintLadder: Count the corners and sides.
Does it have flat or curved faces?
Think about what the shape looks like from different angles.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Use direct and indirect comparison to measure length, mass and capacity
hintLadder: Line up one end of each object.
Which one has more/heavier/fills more?
Use the same unit for both measurements.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Identify and continue repeating patterns and create number patterns using addition and skip counting
hintLadder: Find the part that repeats.
How many terms before it starts again?
Can you predict the next number?

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Collect and represent data in lists, tables and simple picture graphs and interpret results
hintLadder: Count the pictures or marks in each row.
Which group has the most/least?
Read the title and labels before answering.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Read and represent time to the hour and half-hour on analogue and digital clocks
hintLadder: The short hand shows the hour.
Where is the long hand pointing?
Half past means the long hand is on the 6.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Read, write and represent three-digit numbers and explain the place value of each digit
hintLadder: Start with the hundreds blocks.
Count the remaining tens and ones.
Write hundreds, then tens, then ones.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Apply addition and subtraction strategies to solve problems within 100 including regrouping
hintLadder: Add the ones first.
Do you need to regroup? Can you make a ten?
Check: does your answer make sense?

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Represent and solve multiplication problems using groups, arrays and repeated addition for 2, 3, 5 and 10 times tables
hintLadder: Count the equal groups.
How many in each group?
Write it as repeated addition first.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Recognise, model and describe equal sharing and equal grouping as division
hintLadder: Share equally one at a time.
How many groups of that size can you make?
What multiplication fact could help?

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Recognise and represent half and quarter as equal parts of a whole and a collection
hintLadder: Are the parts equal in size?
How many equal parts make the whole?
Colour one part to show a fraction.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Measure and compare length, area, mass and capacity using standard and non-standard units
hintLadder: Make sure you start measuring from zero.
Use the same unit for both objects.
Record the number and the unit name.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Read and represent time to the quarter-hour and understand AM and PM
hintLadder: Quarter past means 15 minutes after the hour.
Quarter to means 15 minutes before the next hour.
Think about whether it is morning or afternoon.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Identify and describe the properties of 2D shapes and 3D objects including symmetry and transformation
hintLadder: Fold the shape in half — do both sides match?
Can you slide, flip or turn this shape to match the other?
Name the shape by its properties, not its position.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Collect, organise and display data in tables, picture graphs and bar graphs and draw conclusions
hintLadder: Read the scale on the side.
Find the bar for each category.
Compare bar heights to answer the question.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Read, write and represent four-digit numbers and apply place value understanding including rounding to the nearest 10 and 100
hintLadder: Look at the digit in the place you are rounding to.
What is the digit to the right?
If it is 5 or more, round up; less than 5, round down.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Apply written strategies for addition and subtraction of up to four-digit numbers
hintLadder: Line up the digits by place value.
Start adding or subtracting from the ones column.
Regroup when a column total is 10 or more.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Recall multiplication facts up to 10x10 and apply them to solve problems
hintLadder: Think of a related fact you know.
Use skip counting to check.
Write out the times table to find the pattern.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Apply division facts related to multiplication tables and solve simple division problems with remainders
hintLadder: Which multiplication fact is closest?
How many are left over after equal groups?
Write the answer as quotient and remainder.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Model, compare and order unit fractions with the same denominator and place them on a number line
hintLadder: Divide the whole into equal parts first.
The bottom number tells how many equal parts.
The top number tells how many you are counting.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Measure perimeter and area of rectangles using grids and the standard formula
hintLadder: Count the squares inside for area.
Add up all the sides for perimeter.
Label your answer with the correct units.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Read and interpret data in picture graphs, bar graphs and tables including scales greater than one
hintLadder: Check the scale: each unit represents how many?
Multiply the bar height by the scale value.
Read the question carefully before answering.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Describe the likelihood of events using the language of chance including impossible, unlikely, likely and certain
hintLadder: Could this event ever happen?
Is it more or less likely than the other event?
Place the event on the scale from impossible to certain.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Describe location and direction using grid references, compass directions and mapping conventions
hintLadder: Go across first, then up — across the corridor then up the stairs.
Use the compass rose to find directions.
Name the column letter then the row number.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Read, write and compare large numbers up to millions and apply flexible place value understanding
hintLadder: Separate the digits into groups of three from the right.
Name the period: thousands, millions, billions.
Read each group name separately.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Apply written strategies for multiplication of two-digit by one-digit numbers using the area model and standard algorithm
hintLadder: Split the two-digit number into tens and ones.
Multiply each part separately.
Add the partial products together.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Investigate and solve problems involving equivalent fractions and locate fractions on a number line
hintLadder: Multiply or divide both numerator and denominator by the same number.
Use the fraction wall to find equivalent strips.
Simplify by finding the greatest common factor.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Recognise and represent decimals to hundredths and connect them to fractions and place value
hintLadder: The tenths place is the first digit after the decimal point.
One tenth = 0.1; one hundredth = 0.01.
Use the hundredths grid to shade the decimal.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Calculate perimeter and area of composite shapes and apply the formulas for rectangles and squares
hintLadder: Split the composite shape into rectangles.
Find the area of each rectangle.
Add them together for the total area.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Create and interpret line graphs for continuous data and compare graphs to make predictions
hintLadder: Read the value at each plotted point.
What does the line going up or down tell you?
Use the trend to predict a future value.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Describe and compare the likelihood of events using fractions and conduct chance experiments
hintLadder: Count the total number of possible outcomes.
Count the favourable outcomes.
Write the probability as a fraction.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Solve problems involving time duration, timetables and the relationship between units of time
hintLadder: Count on in minutes from the start time.
Remember: 60 minutes make 1 hour.
Count the hours, then add the remaining minutes.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Apply efficient strategies for multiplication and division of multi-digit numbers including the standard algorithm
hintLadder: Multiply by the ones digit first.
When multiplying by the tens digit, start one column to the left.
Add the two partial products.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Compare, order and represent fractions with different denominators and convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers
hintLadder: Find a common denominator for both fractions.
Convert to equivalent fractions with the same denominator.
Convert an improper fraction by dividing numerator by denominator.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Add and subtract fractions with related denominators and multiply fractions by whole numbers
hintLadder: Convert to the same denominator first.
Add or subtract only the numerators.
Simplify the result by dividing by the common factor.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Represent and compare decimals to thousandths and add and subtract decimals
hintLadder: Line up the decimal points before adding.
Use zeros as placeholders where needed.
Check: does the decimal point in the answer line up?

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Understand and apply percentages as rates per hundred and connect to fractions and decimals
hintLadder: Per cent means per hundred.
Convert the fraction to an equivalent fraction over 100.
Move the decimal point two places to convert decimal to percent.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Explore the Cartesian plane and graph and interpret relationships between variables
hintLadder: The x-axis goes left and right, the y-axis goes up and down.
Read the x value first, then the y value.
Plot the point at the intersection of x and y.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Calculate mean, median, mode and range and select appropriate measure of centre for a data set
hintLadder: Sort the data from smallest to largest.
The median is the middle value.
The mean is the sum divided by the count.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Solve problems involving volume and capacity of rectangular prisms using formal units
hintLadder: Count the cubes in one layer.
How many layers are there?
Multiply length by width by height.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Apply order of operations (BODMAS) to evaluate and write numerical expressions with brackets
hintLadder: Evaluate inside brackets first.
Then work out any multiplication or division.
Finally, add or subtract from left to right.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Solve problems involving fractions, decimals and percentages in real-world contexts
hintLadder: Convert the percentage to a decimal or fraction.
Multiply the quantity by the fraction or decimal.
Check: does the answer make sense in context?

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Identify and describe properties of prime and composite numbers and apply divisibility rules
hintLadder: List all the numbers that divide evenly into it.
A prime has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Use divisibility rules to test 2, 3, 5, 10 first.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Investigate and solve problems involving ratios and rates in everyday contexts
hintLadder: Write the ratio as a fraction.
Multiply both parts by the same number to scale up.
Check: do both parts stay in proportion?

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Write, evaluate and interpret algebraic expressions and equations using pronumerals
hintLadder: The pronumeral represents an unknown value.
Write the expression using the given information.
Solve by doing the same thing to both sides.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Calculate angles in triangles and on straight lines and classify triangles by their properties
hintLadder: Angles in a triangle always add to 180°.
Angles on a straight line add to 180°.
Subtract the known angles to find the unknown.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Interpret and critically evaluate statistical data and identify misleading representations
hintLadder: Check the scale: does it start at zero?
Is the sample size large enough?
Look for ways the graph might be misleading.

nodes.subject: maths
nodes.objective: Assign and compare probabilities of complementary and mutually exclusive events
hintLadder: The probability of an event not happening = 1 minus the probability it happens.
Mutually exclusive events cannot both occur.
List all outcomes and mark the favourable ones.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Apply knowledge of grapheme-phoneme correspondences to decode unfamiliar words in simple texts
hintLadder: Say each sound in the word from left to right.
Blend the sounds together smoothly.
Does the word make sense in the sentence?

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Read and spell high-frequency words including common irregular words (sight words)
hintLadder: Look at the whole word shape.
Say the word aloud and remember it.
Find it in a sentence you know.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Comprehend a short text by identifying the main idea and supporting details
hintLadder: What is the whole text mostly about?
Find the sentence that best sums it up.
Supporting details give extra information about the main idea.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Write simple grammatically correct sentences with capital letters, full stops and question marks
hintLadder: Every sentence starts with a capital letter.
A telling sentence ends with a full stop.
A question ends with a question mark.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Identify and use nouns, verbs, adjectives and pronouns in sentences
hintLadder: A noun names a person, place or thing.
A verb is an action or state.
An adjective describes a noun.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Spell simple words using knowledge of common spelling patterns and CVC, CVCE and consonant blend structures
hintLadder: Say the word slowly and write each sound.
Check: does the word look right?
Use a word you know that has the same pattern.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Listen and respond to spoken texts by predicting, retelling and asking questions
hintLadder: Think about what happened first, next and last.
Use what you heard to predict what might happen.
Ask a question about something you want to know more about.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Read texts with fluency and expression, applying decoding strategies for multisyllabic words
hintLadder: Break long words into syllables.
Read phrases smoothly, not word by word.
Read with expression to show how characters feel.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Comprehend narrative and informational texts by making inferences and identifying the author's purpose
hintLadder: An inference is when you use clues from the text plus what you know.
Why did the author write this — to inform, persuade or entertain?
Find evidence in the text to support your answer.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Write a structured recount or narrative with a beginning, middle and end using time connectives
hintLadder: Start with who, when and where.
Use words like first, then, next and finally.
End with a conclusion or resolution.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Spell words applying common digraphs, blends, long vowel patterns and morphological patterns including plurals and simple suffixes
hintLadder: Does the base word end in e? Drop the e before adding -ing.
If the noun ends in s, x, ch or sh, add -es for plural.
Check the spelling pattern against a word family.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Identify and use simple punctuation including commas in lists, exclamation marks and apostrophes for contractions
hintLadder: An apostrophe in a contraction replaces the missing letter.
Commas separate items in a list.
An exclamation mark shows strong feeling.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Understand and use text features of informational texts including headings, subheadings and captions
hintLadder: Headings tell you the topic of each section.
Captions explain pictures or diagrams.
Use the subheadings to find information quickly.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Analyse literary texts for character, setting and plot structure and identify how language creates meaning
hintLadder: What do the character's words and actions tell you about them?
What words does the author use to describe the setting?
How does the structure affect how you feel as a reader?

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Write informational texts using topic sentences, supporting details and a concluding statement
hintLadder: Start each paragraph with a topic sentence.
Add at least two supporting details.
End with a sentence that links back to the main idea.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Spell words using morphological knowledge including prefixes, suffixes and base words
hintLadder: Find the base word first.
Does the suffix change the spelling of the base?
Double the final consonant when the base ends CVC and the suffix starts with a vowel.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Identify and apply knowledge of sentence types including statements, questions, commands and exclamations
hintLadder: A command starts with a verb.
A question asks something and ends with ?.
An exclamation shows strong emotion and ends with !.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Discuss vocabulary and use context clues to determine the meaning of unfamiliar words and phrases
hintLadder: Read the sentences around the unknown word.
What makes sense in that gap?
Check the meaning by substituting your guess.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Speak clearly in structured presentations with awareness of audience and purpose
hintLadder: Plan your key points before speaking.
Speak loudly and clearly so everyone can hear.
Look at your audience as you speak.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Compare and contrast information from multiple texts and evaluate the reliability of sources
hintLadder: Who wrote this and why?
What evidence does each source give?
Do both sources agree or disagree on the key facts?

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Write persuasive texts using a clear position, reasoned arguments and evidence
hintLadder: State your position clearly in the opening.
Support each argument with a reason and evidence.
Finish with a strong conclusion restating your position.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Spell a range of words including homophones, commonly confused words and words with Latin and Greek roots
hintLadder: Homophones sound the same but have different meanings.
Think about the meaning, not just the sound.
The root often gives a clue about the word's meaning.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Use complex sentences with subordinate clauses and a variety of conjunctions to improve writing
hintLadder: A subordinate clause cannot stand alone.
Use conjunctions like because, although, when, if.
Put the subordinate clause before or after the main clause.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Understand and apply different types of figurative language including simile, metaphor and personification
hintLadder: A simile uses like or as to compare.
A metaphor says something IS something else.
Personification gives human qualities to non-human things.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Plan, draft, revise and edit written texts using feedback to improve clarity, vocabulary and organisation
hintLadder: Read your draft aloud — does it make sense?
Does each paragraph have a clear topic?
Check vocabulary: can you use a more precise word?

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Analyse how authors use narrative structure, point of view and language choices to create impact
hintLadder: Who is telling this story?
What effect does the author's word choice have on you?
How would this scene feel different with a different narrator?

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Write and refine informational and persuasive texts using sophisticated vocabulary, varied sentence structures and text organisation
hintLadder: Vary your sentence length — mix short and long sentences.
Choose precise vocabulary to convey your exact meaning.
Check: does the structure match the purpose of the text?

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Identify and explain the effect of grammatical choices including tense, voice and modal verbs
hintLadder: Active voice: subject does the action. Passive: subject receives it.
Modal verbs (might, must, should) show degree of certainty.
Consistent tense maintains the time frame of the text.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Comprehend complex texts by synthesising information, identifying bias and evaluating author's argument
hintLadder: Is the author using facts or opinions?
Does the author present both sides or only one?
What evidence is given? Is it reliable?

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Use a dictionary and thesaurus to expand vocabulary, understand etymology and select words for effect
hintLadder: Check the dictionary definition, not just the synonym list.
Consider the connotation: positive, negative or neutral?
The etymology can reveal the word's root meaning.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Analyse how texts position readers through language, structure and perspective choices including critical literacy
hintLadder: Who benefits from this text being written this way?
What is left out or downplayed?
What language choices position you to agree with the author?

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Plan, draft and produce a polished extended written text demonstrating control of structure, language and conventions
hintLadder: Use a planning frame to organise your ideas first.
Use linking words to connect paragraphs.
Edit for purpose, audience and the effect on the reader.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Investigate how language evolves over time and across contexts including formal and informal registers
hintLadder: Consider the audience and purpose — is it formal or informal?
Look for contractions, slang or technical vocabulary.
How does the register change the relationship with the reader?

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Conduct and present a structured research inquiry using multiple sources with proper referencing
hintLadder: Read, close the source, then write in your own words.
Paraphrase means say the same idea differently.
Note the author, title and date for each source.

nodes.subject: english
nodes.objective: Engage in collaborative discussion using active listening, respectful disagreement and building on others' ideas
hintLadder: Listen carefully before responding.
You can agree and add, or politely disagree with a reason.
Invite others with: 'What do you think about...?'
